existing_assessments:
LITMUS sentence repetition (SRep) task for Palestinian Arabic
Developed by Armon-Lotem and Saiegh-Haddad (Bar-Ilan), with Haj Yahye and Halabi
SRep reported highly sensitive and specific; LITMUS built for multilingual children
Records that the instrument exists — not that any service here uses it
existing_multilingualProvision: Not established from the sources consulted — a language-appropriate LITMUS sentence repetition instrument exists for this system (see assessments above), but whether any service, clinical guideline or funder requires, supports or reimburses assessment in all of a child's languages was not determined. That gap between an available research instrument and routine clinical practice is the single most useful thing a contributor here could resolve.

docLinks.label: UNESCO GEM Report, Profiles Enhancing Education Reviews (PEER), Yemen: Inclusion

existing_terminology:
Working term is "special needs", paired in the source with "different handicaps"
2013-15 Mid Term Results Framework counted 120,721 such pupils in public schools
"Speech Education" appears only in an institute name, not as a defined category
PEER finds no definition of inclusive education for Yemen
existing_referralPathway:
Law 61 of 1999 focuses on specialized centres where disabled pupils are educated separately
2015 UNICEF report: schools do not necessarily accept children with disabilities
existing_serviceModel:
No ministry speech or language programme is recorded for Yemen by UNESCO PEER
The only named provision is the Rehabilitation Institute for Special and Speech Education
Its stated intake is mental disability, cerebral palsy and hearing impairment
existing_legalEntitlement:
Law 61/1999 on care and habilitation of the disabled makes education a right for disabled people
1992 Education Law art. 28: the state is to establish special schools and education institutions
Art. 8 of the 1992 Education Law makes education free at all levels, secured gradually
Ministry of Social Affairs must prepare curricula and learning materials for the centres
existing_funding:
Law 2 of 2002 established the National Fund for the Care and Habilitation of the Disabled
Social Fund for Development, Law 10 of 1997, aims to support special-needs education services
existing_workforce:
Law 61 of 1999 has Social Affairs work with universities to prepare specialized educators
Special education faculty at the University of Azal, and a Taiz University department from 2004

docLinks.label: UNESCO PEER, El Salvador — inclusion profile (platform archived; profiles no longer updated)

existing_terminology:
Umbrella term is educacion especial for pupils with special educational needs
Ley General de Educacion defines special education by method, not by category
No speech, language or communication category appears in national policy
Term count on the national inclusion profile: speech 0, language disorder 0
existing_serviceModel:
A Full Time Inclusive School Model was formalised in 2009 after a 2005 pilot
A Department of Inclusive Education sits inside the Ministry of Education
A deputy directorate for the full-time inclusive system was created in 2012
The target is 351 full-time integrated inclusive systems between 2016 and 2026
existing_legalEntitlement:
Special education is free of charge when provided by the state
The 2009 child protection law makes special education free alongside other stages
Placement is in specialised institutions or mainstream centres as needs require
existing_funding:
The CRPD Committee found free state special education was not always the case
The Educated El Salvador Plan proposes incentives for schools and teachers on inclusion
existing_workforce:
No speech and language therapist role appears in national education policy
The ministry has 600 inclusion support teachers for 5,100 public schools
Those teachers serve more than 8,000 pupils with disabilities
existing_outcomesEvidence:
No language-specific figure exists and none can be derived from the school census
18 per cent of disability registrations do not specify the type of disability
2014 school census: 85 per cent of disabled children are in mainstream schools
